en.content: Which of the following oxides of group 16 has the highest boiling point?
en.explanation:
The boiling points of the hydrides of Group 16 elements generally increase down the group due to an increase in molecular size and, consequently, an increase in van der Waals forces among the molecules. However, water ($$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$$) is an exception to this trend because of its ability to form hydrogen bonds, which are much stronger than the dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces that exist in the other hydrides. These hydrogen bonds significantly increase the amount of energy required to break the intermolecular attractions in water, leading to a much higher boiling point for water compared to hydrogen sulfide ($$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{S}$$), hydrogen selenide ($$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se}$$), and hydrogen telluride ($$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}$$).

So, even though under normal circumstances, as you move down the group from oxygen to tellurium, the boiling points of the hydrides increase due to the increase in van der Waals forces, water's unique ability to form extensive hydrogen-bonding networks makes it an exception, giving it the highest boiling point among these hydrides. Thus, the correct answer is:

Option A $$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$$

en.content: Specify the coordination number of cobalt in $$\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)(\mathrm{e n})^2\right]^{2+}$$
en.explanation:
The coordination number of a central metal atom in a complex is determined by the number of ligand donor atoms to which the metal atom is directly bonded. In the complex $$\left[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN})\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)(\mathrm{en})^2\right]^{2+}$$, let's analyze the ligands that are bonded to the cobalt ion:

  • CN (cyanide) - This is a monodentate ligand, contributing 1 donor atom to the coordination number.
  • H2O (water) - This is also a monodentate ligand, contributing 1 donor atom to the coordination number.
  • en (ethylenediamine) - This is a bidentate ligand, meaning each molecule of en contributes 2 donor atoms to the coordination number. Since there are 2 en ligands, they contribute a total of 4 donor atoms.

Adding up the donor atoms:

  • CN: 1 donor atom
  • H2O: 1 donor atom
  • 2 en: 4 donor atoms (2 per ligand)

Thus, the total coordination number of cobalt in the complex is $$1 + 1 + 4 = 6$$. Therefore, the correct answer is:

Option A: 6

en.content: When an electrolytic solution conducts electricity, the current is carried by
en.explanation:
When an electrolytic solution conducts electricity, the current is indeed carried by the movement of ions within the solution. An electrolytic solution is made when an electrolyte dissolves in water or another solvent, dissociating into its constituent ions. These ions are charged particles: cations (positively charged) and anions (negatively charged).

Cations migrate towards the cathode (the negative electrode), and anions migrate towards the anode (the positive electrode) under the influence of an electric field in the solution. This movement of ions constitutes the electric current in the solution. Thus, Option B - cations and anions - is the correct answer. Electrons do not carry the current in the solution itself; instead, they move through the external circuit connecting the anode and cathode. Neutral molecules and the atoms of the electrolyte do not play a direct role in conducting electricity in the solution.

Identify B in the following series of reaction

en.explanation:
The given reaction sequence involves a Grignard reaction followed by an acidic workup. Let's break down each step:

Step 1: Grignard Reaction

The Grignard reagent, $$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{MgX}$$, is a strong nucleophile. It attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of acetaldehyde ($$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}$$). This results in the formation of an alkoxide intermediate, which upon acidic workup (with water, $$\mathrm{HOH}$$) gives the corresponding alcohol.

The reaction can be represented as follows:

$$ \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO} + \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{MgX} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH(OMgX)CH}_3 $$

Step 2: Acidic Workup

The alkoxide intermediate reacts with water to form the final product, an alcohol. The reaction can be represented as follows:

$$ \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH(OMgX)CH}_3 + \mathrm{HOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH(OH)CH}_3 + \mathrm{MgXOH} $$

The product formed is 2-propanol. Therefore, B is 2-propanol.

Correct Answer: Option A

en.direction: Complete the sentence in the following questions with most appropriate choice.
en.content: I can write with .............. hand.
en.explanation:
The sentence "I can write with .............. hand." is a reference to the ability to use one of two hands, or possibly both hands, for writing. Thus, the most appropriate completion of the sentence should indicate the capability to use any one of the two hands (left or right) or both. The choices are analyzed as follows:

  • Option A - every: This option is not suitable because "every" is used to refer to all members of a group of three or more. Since the sentence is about writing with a hand, and individuals typically have two hands, "every" is not the right choice.

  • Option B - two: "Two" is also incorrect because it literally implies writing with two hands simultaneously, which, although possible, is not the common interpretation or intention behind the statement.

  • Option C - either: This is the most appropriate choice. "Either" correctly implies a choice between two distinct alternatives, in this case, the left hand or the right hand, without stating a preference for one over the other. It conveys the ability to write with one hand, with the choice being open.

  • Option D - both: "Both" indicates the use of two things together. While it's true some people might be able to write with both hands (ambidexterity), the statement aiming to be more general and inclusive of all individuals' abilities would best be served by indicating the potential to use one hand or the other.

Therefore, the correct completion for the sentence is Option C - either, which makes the complete sentence: "I can write with either hand."

en.content: We bought ............. books.

The sentence "We bought ............. books." requires a word that can appropriately modify the noun "books" in a way that relates to quantity because "books" is a countable noun. Let's look at the options provided:

  • Option A - much: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns to indicate a large quantity, so it is not suitable for countable nouns like "books."

  • Option B - more: "More" is used to indicate a comparative quantity or degree. Without any context for comparison, "more" alone does not complete the sentence appropriately.

  • Option C - any: "Any" is usually used in questions and negative statements, not typically for affirmative statements to indicate quantity.

  • Option D - many: "Many" is used with countable nouns to indicate a large quantity. It fits perfectly in the context of the sentence, which talks about purchasing a quantity of books.

Therefore, the most appropriate choice to complete the sentence is Option D - many. The completed sentence should read: "We bought many books."

en.content: Select the antonym for the word 'Bane'.
en.explanation:
The word 'bane' refers to something that causes great distress, ruin, or harm. Therefore, we're looking for an antonym that represents a positive or beneficial influence, the opposite of distress or harm.

  • Option A: Boom - This can refer to a period of rapid growth, economic success, or increased popularity. Considering the definition of 'bane,' 'Boom' is a suitable antonym because it implies positive outcomes or benefits, which is the exact opposite of harm or ruin. Therefore, Boom is the correct antonym.

  • Option B: Commotion - This refers to a state of confusion and disorder. It does not directly contrast with the notion of causing distress or harm as 'bane' does, thus not a suitable antonym.

  • Option C: Penance - This is an act of self-punishment or religious discipline to atone for one's sins or wrongdoings. It does not embody the opposite concept of causing harm or distress; therefore, it is not the correct antonym.

  • Option D: Curse - This actually synonymizes with 'bane,' as both imply something that causes harm or misfortune. As such, it cannot be the antonym.

Given these definitions, Option A: Boom is the correct antonym for 'bane' as it represents a positive impact or state of flourishing, which is the opposite of bane's implication of harm or distress.

en.content: Pick out the correct synonym of the word 'Treason'.

'Treason' refers to the crime of betraying one's country, especially by attempting to kill the sovereign or overthrow the government. The essence of this term lies in the act of betrayal or disloyalty to one's nation or its principles. Thus, 'Disloyalty', which means a lack of loyalty or faithfulness, closely aligns with the conceptual meaning of 'Treason' more than the other options provided.

Option B, 'Passion', means a strong and barely controllable emotion, which doesn't relate to the betrayal or political context of treason. en.content: Evaluate $$\int \frac{3 x-2}{(x+3)(x+1)^2} d x$$.
en.explanation:
Let $$I=\int \frac{3 x-2}{(x+3)(x+1)^2} d x$$

By partial fraction

$$\begin{aligned} & \frac{(3 x-2)}{(x+3)(x+1)^2}=\frac{A}{x+3}+\frac{B}{(x+1)}+\frac{C}{(x+1)^2} \quad\text{....(i)} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & (3 x-2)=A(x+1)^2+B(x+3)(x+1)+C(x+3) \\ & =A\left(x^2+1+2 x\right)+B\left(x^2+4 x+3\right)+C(x+3) \\ & (A+B) x^2+(2 A+4 B+C) x+(A+3 B+3 C)\end{aligned}$$

On comparing the like powers of $$x$$, we get

$$\begin{aligned} & A+B=0 \quad \text{.... (ii)}\\ & 2 A+4 B+C=3 \quad \text{.... (iii)}\\ & \text { and } \quad A+3 B+3 C=-2 \quad \text{.... (iv)}\\ \end{aligned}$$

On multiplying Eq. (iii) by 3 and then subtracting it from Eq. (iv), we get

From Eqs. (ii) and (v), we get

$$B=\frac{11}{4} \text { and } A=\frac{-11}{4}$$

From Eq. (iii),

$$\begin{aligned} C & =3-2 A-4 B \\ & =3-2\left(\frac{-11}{4}\right)-4\left(\frac{11}{4}\right) \\ & =3+\frac{22}{4}-\frac{44}{4}=3-\frac{22}{4}=3-\frac{11}{2} \\ & =-\frac{5}{2} \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore$$ From Eq. (i), we get

$$\begin{aligned} & \frac{(3 x-2)}{(x+3)(x+1)^2}=\frac{-11}{4(x+3)}+\frac{11}{4(x+1)} \cdot \frac{-5}{2(x+1)^2} \\ \Rightarrow & \int \frac{(3 x-2)}{(x+3)(x+1)^2} d x \\ = & \int\left\{\frac{-11}{4(x+3)}+\frac{11}{4(x+1)}-\frac{5}{2(x+1)^2}\right\} d x \\ = & -\frac{11}{4} \log |x+3|+\frac{11}{4} \log |x+1|+\frac{5}{2(x+1)}+C \\ = & \frac{11}{4} \log \left|\frac{x+1}{x+3}\right|+\frac{5}{2(x+1)}+C \end{aligned}$$

en.content: Five persons entered the lift cabin on the ground floor of an eight floor house. Suppose that each of them independently and with equal probability can leave the cabin at any floor beginning with the first, then the probability of all 5 persons leaving at different floors is
en.explanation:
To find the probability that all 5 persons leave at different floors beginning from the first floor in an eight-floor house, let's break the solution into steps:

Firstly, there are 7 possible floors where each person can get off (not considering the ground floor, since that's where they are starting). Since we want each of the 5 persons to exit on different floors, we're essentially selecting 5 floors out of these 7 and ordering them (because the order in which they get off matters - which person gets off on which floor).

The number of ways to select and order 5 floors out of 7 is given by the permutation formula, which is:

$$\text{{Number of permutations}} = {}^7P_5 = \frac{7!}{(7-5)!} = \frac{7!}{2!}$$

This calculation gives us the number of favorable outcomes - the different ways in which the 5 persons can exit on 5 different floors.

To find the total number of outcomes (favorable and non-favorable), note that each person can choose to exit on any of the 7 floors independently. So for each person, there are 7 choices, making the total number of outcomes for 5 people:

$$\text{{Total outcomes}} = 7^5$$

The probability of all 5 persons leaving the cabin on different floors can then be calculated as the ratio of the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of outcomes:

$$\text{{Probability}} = \frac{\text{{Number of favorable outcomes}}}{\text{{Total outcomes}}} = \frac{{}^7P_5}{7^5}$$

Hence, the correct option is:

Option A: $$\frac{{}^7P_5}{7^5}$$

en.content: The quotient of the identity function by the reciprocal function is given by
en.explanation:
To solve this problem, let's understand the functions involved and then solve for the quotient of the given functions.

The identity function is a function that always returns the same value that was used as its input. It is defined as $$f(x) = x.$$

The reciprocal function is a function that returns the reciprocal (or multiplicative inverse) of the input value. It is defined as $$g(x) = \frac{1}{x},$$ where $x \neq 0$ because the reciprocal of zero is undefined.

Now, the quotient of the identity function by the reciprocal function would be calculated by dividing $f(x)$ by $g(x)$. Formally, this quotient, let's call it $h(x)$, is calculated as:

$$h(x) = \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$$

Substituting $f(x) = x$ and $g(x) = \frac{1}{x}$, we get:

$$h(x) = \frac{x}{\frac{1}{x}}$$

To simplify $h(x)$, remember that dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal. Therefore, we have:

$$h(x) = x \cdot x = x^2$$

This calculation is valid only for $x \in \mathbb{R}-\{0\}$, as $g(x)$ is undefined at $x = 0$. Therefore, the quotient of the identity function by the reciprocal function is $x^2$ for all real numbers except zero.

This matches Option C:

$$x^2 \forall x \in \mathbb{R}-\{0\}$$

en.content: Which of the following is not a function?
en.explanation:
To determine which of the given options is not a function, we need to recall the definition of a function in the context of sets of ordered pairs. A set of ordered pairs is a function if, for every $x$ in the domain, there is exactly one $y$ in the codomain corresponding to $x$. This means that each input ($x$ value) must map to only one output ($y$ value). Let's analyze each option based on this criterion.

Option A: $$\left\{(x, y): x, y \in \mathbb{R}, x^2=y\right\}$$

This is a function because for each $x$ value, there is exactly one $y$ value such that $y = x^2$. This relationship passes the vertical line test, as no vertical line can intersect the graph at more than one point. Thus, Option A is indeed a function.

Option B: $$\left\{(x, y): x, y \in \mathbb{R}, y^2=x\right\}$$

This option is not a function. The reason is that for a given $x$ (except for $x=0$), there can be two different $y$ values such that $y^2=x$: one positive and one negative. For example, if $x=4$, both $y=2$ and $y=-2$ satisfy the equation $y^2=x$. This violates the definition of a function since one $x$ value corresponds to more than one $y$ value. Therefore, Option B is not a function.

Option C: $$\left\{(x, y): x, y \in \mathbb{R}, x=y^3\right\}$$

This is a function because for each $y$ value, there is exactly one $x$ value that can be calculated using $x = y^3$. No matter what $y$ value you choose, plugging it into $y^3$ will yield one unique $x$, making it a function.

Option D: $$\left\{(x, y): x, y \in \mathbb{R}, y=x^3\right\}$$

This also describes a function. For every $x$ value, $y = x^3$ produces a single $y$ value. This equation satisfies the function criterion as each input ($x$) has exactly one output ($y$).

Therefore, the correct answer to which of the following is not a function is Option B:

$$\left\{(x, y): x, y \in \mathbb{R}, y^2=x\right\}$$

So that, $$(x+i y)^2+|x+i y|=0 \quad$$ [from Eq. (i)]

$$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad x^2-y^2+2 i x y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left(x^2-y^2+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\right)+i(2 x y)=0 \end{aligned}$$

$$x^2-y^2+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=0 \quad \text{.... (ii)}$$

and $$2 x y=0 \Rightarrow x=0$$ or $$y=0\quad \text{.... (iii)}$$

en.content: The Brewster's law is given by the expression
en.explanation:
The correct option for Brewster's Law is:

Option B $$\mu=\tan \theta_p$$

Brewster's law relates the refractive index of a material to the angle of polarization, denoted as $\theta_p$, at which light with a particular polarization is perfectly transmitted through a transparent dielectric surface, with no reflection. When light hits the surface at this angle, the reflected light is perfectly polarized perpendicular to the plane of incidence. Mathematically, Brewster's law is given by:

$$\mu = \tan \theta_p$$

where $\mu$ is the refractive index of the material and $\theta_p$ is the Brewster's angle. According to this law, $\mu$ is the tangent of the Brewster's angle ($\theta_p$), which is the angle of incidence at which light with its electric vector perpendicular to the incidence plane (p-polarized) is not reflected.

The other options given are representations of different laws or relationships in physics, not Brewster's law. For instance, Option A represents Snell's law of refraction, expressed incorrectly here as the correct form would be $\mu = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index, $i$ is the angle of incidence, and $r$ is the angle of refraction. en.content: The demodulator or detector circuit consists of a
en.explanation:
The correct answer is Option C: diode.

In the context of radio and signal processing, a demodulator or detector's primary function is to extract or retrieve the information signal from the modulated carrier wave. This process involves converting the variations in amplitude, frequency, or phase of the carrier into a form that can be more easily used, often transforming the signal back to its original form or to a form that can be further processed.

A diode plays a crucial role in many types of demodulation circuits because of its unique ability to allow current to flow in one direction while blocking it in the opposite direction. This property makes the diode particularly useful in demodulating amplitude-modulated (AM) signals, among others. For example, in AM demodulation, a diode can be used to rectify the incoming modulated signal, allowing only the positive (or negative, depending on the orientation) halves of the waves to pass through. When combined with a capacitor to filter the result, this effectively extracts the modulation envelope, which carries the original information content of the signal.

The other options, while important in various electronics circuits, do not directly serve the primary function of a demodulator:

  • Resistor (Option A): Used to control current or divide voltages in electronic circuits, not specifically for demodulation.
  • Transistor (Option B): Acts as a switch or amplifier in electronics. It can be part of a demodulator circuit but is not the key component for the demodulation process itself.
  • Capacitor (Option D): Stores electrical energy temporarily and can help filter or smooth out the signal after demodulation but is not the principal component for extracting the signal from a modulated waveform.

en.content: The power $$(P)$$ of an engine lifting a mass of $$100 \mathrm{~kg}$$ upto a height of $$10 \mathrm{~m}$$ in $$1 \mathrm{~min}$$ is
en.explanation:
To calculate the power required to lift a mass, we use the formula:

$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$

where:

  • $P$ is the power in watts,
  • $W$ is the work done in joules, and
  • $t$ is the time in seconds.

The work done in lifting an object is equal to the potential energy gained by the object, which can be calculated by the formula:

$$W = mgh$$

where:

  • $m$ is the mass in kilograms,
  • $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity ($9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2$), and
  • $h$ is the height in meters.

Given that:

  • $m = 100 \, \text{kg}$,
  • $h = 10 \, \text{m}$, and
  • $t = 1 \, \text{min} = 60 \, \text{seconds}$ (since time needs to be in seconds for the formula).

First, we calculate the work done:

$$W = (100 \, \text{kg}) \times (9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2) \times (10 \, \text{m}) = 9800 \, \text{J}$$

Then, we find the power:

$$P = \frac{9800 \, \text{J}}{60 \, \text{s}} = 163.3 \, \text{W}$$

Therefore, the power of the engine is $163.3 \, \text{W}$, which corresponds to Option A: P = 163.3 W.

en.content: An electron revolves in a circle at the rate of $$10^{19}$$ rounds per second. The equivalent current is $$\left(e=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}\right)$$
en.explanation:
The equivalent current produced by an electron revolving in a circle can be calculated by taking into account the charge of the electron and the rate at which it makes rounds per second.

The formula to calculate current ($$I$$) in this context is given by:

$I = n\cdot e$

where:

  • $$n$$ is the number of electrons passing a given point per second, and in this case, it's equivalent to the number of rounds made by a single electron per second because it's only one electron.
  • $$e$$ is the charge of an electron ($$1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{Coulombs}$$).

Given that the electron makes $$10^{19}$$ rounds per second, we have:

$n = 10^{19} \, \text{rounds per second}$

Therefore, to find the current, we substitute $$n$$ and $$e$$ into the formula:

$I = n\cdot e = 10^{19} \cdot 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$

$I = 1.6 \, \text{A}$

So, the equivalent current is 1.6 A. Hence, the correct answer is Option B: 1.6 A.

en.content: An electric charge does not have which of the following properties?
en.explanation:
The correct option that represents a property not associated with an electric charge is Option D: Circular line of force.

Let's examine each option closely to understand why:

Option A: Total charge conservation - This principle states that the total charge in an isolated system remains constant. This is a fundamental property of electric charge, governed by the law of conservation of charge. It means that in any process, the sum of all the electric charges before the process equals the sum of all the electric charges after the process, indicating that electric charge cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred from one body to another.

Option B: Quantisation of charge - The quantization of charge means that the charge on an object is always an integer multiple of the elementary charge (e), where \(e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \) Coulombs. No matter how small, a charge can’t be a fraction of this elementary charge, thus demonstrating that charge is quantized.

Option C: Two types of charge - There are indeed two types of electric charges: positive and negative. This dichotomy is foundational to the structure of electromagnetism, where like charges repel each other and opposite charges attract each other. This property is fundamental to the behavior of charged particles and underlies practically all electric phenomena.

Option D: Circular line of force - Electric lines of force or electric field lines emanating from a charged particle are radial and straight, originating from positive charges and ending at negative charges. They are not circular in nature under normal circumstances. The concept of circular lines of force is more appropriately linked to magnetic fields around a current-carrying conductor or the magnetic field of a bar magnet, not to electric charges directly. Therefore, Option D is a property that does not belong to electric charges.

en.content: Which component of electromagnetic spectrum have maximum wavelength?
en.explanation:
The electromagnetic spectrum encompasses a wide range of electromagnetic radiation types, ranging from very short wavelengths (like gamma rays) to very long wavelengths (like radio waves). The correct answer to the question of which component of the electromagnetic spectrum has the maximum wavelength is:

Option A: Radio waves

Explanation:

The electromagnetic spectrum is organized by wavelength and frequency. The spectrum is usually divided from the shortest wavelengths (and highest frequencies and energies) to the longest wavelengths (and lowest frequencies and energies). Here’s a brief overview, from shortest to longest wavelength:

  • Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength and the most energy.
  • X-rays follow, with slightly longer wavelengths than gamma rays but shorter than those of ultraviolet light.
  • The visible spectrum, which is the range of wavelengths perceptible to the human eye, falls in the middle of the electromagnetic spectrum. This includes all the colors from violet to red.
  • Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the electromagnetic spectrum. They can range from the size of a football to much larger than our planet, depending on their frequency.

Therefore, radio waves (Option A) have the maximum wavelength among the options provided, making them the correct answer.
